text_blocks.snippet: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs (alveoli) in one or both lungs, causing them to fill with fluid or pus. The disease process involves the invasion of pathogens, triggering an immune response that leads to inflammation and fluid buildup in the lungs, impairing oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange.
snippet_highlighted_words: involves the invasion of pathogens, triggering an immune response that leads to inflammation and fluid buildup in the lungs, impairing oxygen and carbon dioxide exchange

list.snippet: Pneumonia typically begins when pathogens, like bacteria or viruses, enter the lungs.
These pathogens can enter through various routes, including aspiration (inhaling foreign material), inhalation of infectious droplets, or hematogenous spread (through the bloodstream).
The pathogens then colonize the pharynx and potentially the lower respiratory tract.
The body's immune system detects the pathogens and sends white blood cells, particularly neutrophils, to the site of infection.
These white blood cells, along with fluid and cellular debris, accumulate in the alveoli, causing inflammation and consolidation.
